item.title: Oxford’s ice rink and light walk reopen Friday with an 8:30 p.m. last entry
item.description: Families heading to mTrade Park in Oxford can skate or walk the lights Friday through Sunday, November 27–29, 2026, following the Thanksgiving Day closure. Visit Oxford lists hours of 5 to 9 p.m. at both attractions. The last ticket sale and entry are at 8:30 p.m., half an hour before closing. The park is at 4259 Old Sardis Road. Oxford on Ice uses a 4,000-square-foot outdoor ice rink. Visit Oxford lists skating admission at $5 and Walk of Lights admission at $10. Each attraction lists free entry for children ages three and younger. Rink visitors must sign a waiver. Skaters age 18 or younger must have an adult with them. Bring socks because there are none for sale on site. Visitors can park free at mTrade Park. Visit Oxford says the Walk of Lights follows concrete or asphalt paths. The regular schedule is Wednesday through Sunday through January 3, 2027. The holiday schedule closes both attractions on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day. Sources: https://visitoxfordms.com/holly-jolly-oxford/oxford-on-ice/ . https://visitoxfordms.com/holly-jolly-oxford/faq/ . https://visitoxfordms.com/holly-jolly-oxford/walk-of-lights/ . https://visitoxfordms.com/holly-jolly-oxford/ .

item.title: Oxford parade application closes ahead of Dec. 7 celebration on the Square
item.description: Visit Oxford lists the Oxford Christmas Parade for Monday, December 7, 2026, from 6:30 to 8 p.m. on the historic downtown Square. A different date matters for groups planning to enter. The 2026 Christmas Parade Application linked from Visit Oxford displayed a notice that it was no longer accepting responses when checked on Friday, November 27, 2026. Visit Oxford identifies the theme as A Very Oxford Christmas. Its entry notice invited local groups from the Lafayette-Oxford-University community, specified that there was no fee to enter a group and said acceptance depended on approval and the order in which applications came in. The posted application is for groups seeking a place in the parade. Visit Oxford still lists the December 7 event and its hours for spectators. Visit Oxford event listing https://visitoxfordms.com/events/oxford-christmas-parade/ . 2026 Christmas Parade Application https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfIHulT5qjhzEGqI-YsuF_QP6vvLQOXPXsmvzq7bjJvi6b-dA/closedform .
item.source: Visit Oxford and the parade organizers’ registration form

item.title: Lafayette County retail reached 3,359 jobs last December before a January drop
item.description: Saturday, November 28, 2026, is Small Business Saturday, according to the U.S. Small Business Administration. In Lafayette County, federal payroll records show how much local retail employment changed between the last holiday season and the start of 2026. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics counted 3,359 private retail payroll jobs at Lafayette County workplaces in December 2025. That was 222 more jobs than in January 2026, when the bureau counted 3,137. In its first-quarter 2026 file, the bureau recorded 3,248 jobs in February and 3,208 in March. Its figures cover workplaces throughout Lafayette County, including Oxford. Retail employment rose through the final quarter of 2025. The bureau counted 3,278 jobs in October, 3,343 in November and 3,359 in December. December's total was 96 above the 3,263 jobs the bureau reported for December 2024. Retail supplied 3,359 of the county's 18,953 private payroll jobs in December 2025, about 17.7%. The bureau counted 244 private retail establishments during the fourth quarter of 2025, compared with 239 in the fourth quarter of 2024. Average weekly pay per retail job rose from $588 to $618 between those quarters. These records measure employment and pay at local workplaces. U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics county records https://data.bls.gov/cew/data/api/2025/4/area/28071.csv . https://data.bls.gov/cew/data/api/2024/4/area/28071.csv . https://data.bls.gov/cew/data/api/2026/1/area/28071.csv . U.S. Small Business Administration announcement https://legacy.sba.gov/article/2026/11/19/sba-encourages-americans-shop-smallr-small-business-saturdayr-november-28 .

item.title: Grandson gives Ole Miss a copy of The Marble Faun that William Faulkner signed for his grandmother
item.description: The University of Mississippi announced on November 24, 2026, that its Department of Archives and Special Collections in Oxford acquired a family copy of The Marble Faun, William Faulkner’s first commercially published book. Four Seas Co. published the poetry collection in 1924. John Rives of Marietta, Georgia, donated the copy he inherited from his grandmother, Gertrude Stegbauer. Stegbauer worked as a stenographer in the Charleston office of Phil Stone, an Oxford lawyer who was Faulkner’s friend and early literary mentor. The handwritten dedication reads “To Gert, from Bill 19 December 1924.” Faulkner dated it December 19, 1924. Senior curator Jennifer Ford said relatively few copies were printed and that the personal connection gives this one particular significance. Rives wanted the book cared for and knew the university had a Faulkner collection. The department already held other copies with different histories. Bessie Furr, a former classmate of Faulkner, once owned a copy that retained its original dust jacket. That copy became the library’s 1 millionth volume in 1999. Another copy was inscribed to U.S. postal inspector Mark Webster. Interim library dean Gail Herrera said the donated volume would support research and teaching. The department is housed in the J.D. Williams Library on the Oxford campus. Its website offers readers a catalog search, finding aids and researcher registration information. Researchers can consult the department about a visit or request information about its holdings. Archives and Special Collections: https://libraries.olemiss.edu/research-and-collections/archives-and-special-collections/

item.title: Oxford food drive takes cans Tuesday afternoon and at the Thanksgiving Turkey Trot
item.description: The University of Mississippi lists Tuesday, November 24, 2026, from 3:45 p.m. to 6:15 p.m. as the last advance drop-off for canned goods for the 11th Annual Turkey Trot Thanksgiving Fun Run/Walk. Campus Recreation lists both canned-good drop-off and T-shirt pickup in the South Campus Recreation Center lobby in Oxford during the Tuesday afternoon window. On Thursday morning participants can donate and collect a shirt at the South Campus Rail Trail trailhead in Oxford while shirts remain available. Donors may bring 10 canned goods for an event T-shirt, while supplies last. The run and walk are free. Donations benefit Grove Grocery and the Oxford Food Pantry. The official calendar confirms the 11th Annual Turkey Trot Thanksgiving Fun Run/Walk takes place in Oxford on Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, November 26, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 10:30 a.m. Central Standard Time at the South Campus Rail Trail, 980 Whirlpool Drive, Oxford, MS 38655. Participants choose their distance. There is another donation window at the trailhead at 8:30 a.m. on Thursday. Coffee and light refreshments are offered. Campus Recreation lists 662-915-4079 and campusrec@olemiss.edu for accessibility arrangements. The event page links a downloadable calendar for participants: https://eventcalendar.olemiss.edu/event/11th-annual-turkey-trot-thanksgiving-fun-runwalk.ics. Campus Recreation lists Staff Council, the Division of Outreach, Chicory Market, Oxford T-Shirt Company and High Point Coffee as event partners.

item.title: Lafayette County unemployment rises to 3.0% in October
item.description: Lafayette County, Mississippi, including Oxford. The October 2026 preliminary residence-based estimates in the Mississippi Department of Employment Security report put the local unemployment rate at 3.0% in October after a revised 2.4% in September. The August rate was 2.6%. The department counts 30,604 county residents in the October civilian labor force. Of them 29,701 were employed and 903 were unemployed. In September the labor force numbered 30,523, with 29,785 employed and 738 unemployed. The unemployed total rose by 165 residents. The employed count fell by 84. The change in the civilian labor force was +81 people. The survey describes people age 16 and older by where they live. A resident who commutes outside the county remains part of the county residence-based estimates. These counts should not be described as employers adding or eliminating positions. The number unemployed and the number employed together equal the civilian labor force in each month. The comparable Mississippi rate was 3.6%, based on 45,914 unemployed and 1,214,626 employed residents in a civilian labor force of 1,260,540. Both state and county figures in this comparison are unadjusted for seasonal changes. A separate county table in the same release lists 18 initial unemployment insurance claims and 181 continued claims in October compared with 24 initial and 212 continued claims in September. Insurance claims are an administrative measure. They should not be added together or treated as the number of unemployed residents. September is revised and October is preliminary. The tables do not establish what caused any change. The department’s county series gives these monthly rates earlier in 2026: June at 3.2%, July at 3.4%, August at 2.6%, September at 2.4%, October at 3.0%. Source documents: https://mdes.ms.gov/media/23357/labormarketdata.pdf (labor force estimates and county unemployment insurance claims); https://mdes.ms.gov/media/8735/urate.pdf (county monthly unemployment series); https://mdes.ms.gov/media/8654/uratesmapbw.pdf (October county unemployment rate map).
